I think an interesting experiment would be to create voat2.co with the one rule that cross posting is not allowed and mods on Voat may not mod an identically named sub on voat2. The motivation here is basically to see if another sort of identity develops while taking some basic steps to avoid people actively trying to turn it into a clone.

I'd hypothesize that size has a direct influence on the quality of discussion on vote driven social media platforms. Voat2 would be an interesting way to test this out. If this hypothesis turns out to be accurate it may even suggest the idea of creation of a sort of 'bucketed' voat. Multiple subs is now an 'obvious' idea and having a single sub would seem silly, yet Reddit started out a single sub site. Maybe it's the case that running a single instance of the site software is actually a silly limitation and we'd see a substantial improvement in discussion quality were users able to pick less populated servers. And of course those who want the full large-scale social media experience could always just choose to reside on the most populated instance.
